chapter: Uptown versus downtown styles and Tom Anderson's
title: Tom Anderson's place and tips from Norwegian sailors; goodbye
summary: Dawson describes the Basin and Iberville place, bandmates Tom Brown and Sam Moran, tips and gold pieces from sailors; the interview closes.

blocks.x: His place was say a ball, a ballroom you know. And he didn't have much of a dancing space there. About in the Corner of Basin. About in Corner of Basin. About in Corner of Basin in된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된 ! About there you say there after된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된 ! About there you say there after된된된된된된된된된된된된된 된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된 된된된된된된된된된된된 ! About there you say there after된된된된된된된 ! About there된된된된된된된된된된 ! right on the Basin in Iberville. Well did you play there after a man Brown? Tom Brown? Yeah yeah well I played with him. Oh you played with Tom Brown? Yeah Tom Brown. Sam Moran? Sam Moran. What did Tom Brown play? Manlon. Well he was about the best Manlon player by my note. He could read pretty good. Sam Moran? Sam Moran was bass. Sam Moran. Sam Moran. And I was playing guitar with they had two, used two guitars you see. He had a Charlie. Well it's Benard played with him too. He had Snow. Snow played with him a long time. Yeah well he used guitars them times. You know they used two or three guitars sometimes. And the only one. They used to have a Trampon once. They had Ed Jones. Yeah they had Ed Jones. He had Ed Jones playing Trampon on there. That's the only one that was blowing this but he was Jewel. That's the only one. Yeah. That was right on the corner. Now they had a little place in the back where they played every night. But the chips. The salary. You didn't get no salary. You made your money off the tip. But see the tips were so good that we didn't need no salary. That's right. And when we were getting ready to whack up our kitty after knocking off ours then we'd have some time. 10, 12, 15 dollars a piece. All nickels of power. You'd go home loaded. You'd be loaded on more than that sometimes. I seen us make 24 dollars a piece one night. Live you see that time all these chummers used to come off the ship. The Norwegians. They'd come off them ships. The ships used to come in this poacher. And when they'd get in here. They'd have their pockets full of money. They'd just go in the hall. A lot of gold money. I had. We. Now you can tell you. I think it was. A guy put a ten dollar gold piece for a penny in the kitty pocket. And we went to whack up the money. We seen a ten dollar gold piece in there. And they said, this ain't no carpenter. This is a ten dollar gold. And they have a pocket full of money you know. And they said, ah, play there or something. It was something. I don't know. It was terrible. And guys get full of it. They had women you know used to hustle beer in their places you see. And they'd get percentage off of every bottle of beer they sell. What they didn't steal.
Well I think this is just about over here. All right. Certainly enjoyed hearing about the old times. And someday if we think of more questions. stuff
